items.source_quote: a positively (n + 1)-expansive map of the circle which is not positively n-expansive?
items.scope: Every integer n >= 1; continuous selfmaps of the entire circle with a uniform finite strict all-natural-time Bowen bound.

items.source_quote: Which one-dimensional continua admit finitely positively expansive systems?
items.scope: Full classification of one-dimensional continua is not supplied. The circle case is classified in Corollary 8; the cited interval and Hawaiian-earring obstructions and bouquet examples give the neighboring cases.
Preservation by iterates, restrictions and conjugacy; applied in Corollary 9.

Theorem 3.8 excludes finite positive expansivity on a nondegenerate interval. It supplies the interval dependency in Lemma 2; the source interval proof is not claimed as a new result. Remark 3.6 and Lemma 3.7 also supply the antecedent interval selection and doubling method.
The graph-degree inequality is not established by the circle argument.
For 1 <= k <= n a bouquet of n circles supports a positively k-expansive map; for k >= 2 the displayed map is not positively (k-1)-expansive. The full construction is proved in Corollary 10.

items.locator: Proposition 3.11, page 9, and following comment, page 10
items.scope: Hawaiian-earring obstruction and its stated infinite-degree-vertex extension; not reproved here.
Classification of two-sided shifts and substitutive/S-adic systems is separate.
Positive expansivity of the standard power maps of absolute degree at least two; an explicit separation constant is proved in the note.

Corollary 8 proves equivalence with power-map conjugacy from the finite Bowen bound. Under ordinary positive expansivity the classification is classical; Luo-Ntalampekos, arXiv:2411.14203v1 (2024), journal Section 3.4(E2) (2026), records it and cites Coven-Reddy (1980). The latter original chapter is not used as a proof dependency.
If f is finitely positively expansive on a compact metric space and f^p(C) is contained in an embedded circle C, the restriction f^p|C has the same power-map classification, Corollary 9.
Whole-circle homeomorphism subclass already excluded by pointwise two-sided finite expansivity; no unrestricted noninvertible conclusion is inferred from that source.
